reports: Number of parts, part names and instruments, staves per part; layout verdict: SUPPORTED (one pitched part with two staves) or UNSUPPORTED with the reason.
definition: Parts from <part-list>/<score-part>; staves from <attributes><staves>. Only one pitched part with two staves is supported; staff 1 and staff 2 are then the two staves. Every other layout (two parts, one staff, a voice or other instrument part, staves changing mid-piece) is UNSUPPORTED and every per-staff row below returns UNKNOWN for that file instead of guessing.
implementation: Raw MusicXML walk with ElementTree, namespace-agnostic, opening .mxl through META-INF/container.xml (as build_available.py and export_shortlist.py already do). music21 score.parts (two PartStaff objects) as the second reader. Reuse quality_check.not_piano for instrument names.
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: the validators' own raw walk read all 2,020 notated files with 0 errors. music21 gives two PartStaff for a two-staff part; partitura gives one Part with number_of_staves 2 (new-library-research A).
pitfalls: Two parts both named Piano (a right-hand/left-hand split or a duet: several in the 109-file shortlist); voice plus piano (shortlist Ave Maria, part 'Voix'); unnamed parts; a staff added mid-piece.
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: a standard grand-staff file -> SUPPORTED. Fail: a voice-plus-piano file -> UNSUPPORTED (extra part). Fool: two parts, each one staff, both named 'Piano' -> UNSUPPORTED, not merged by guess.
in_our_files: <staff> element present in 714 of 842 (84.8%), a proxy for one part with two staves
used_for: Every row below (precondition); step 4: checking that a generated exercise has the intended layout
why_easy: Direct element read; the only decision is to refuse unusual layouts rather than interpret them.
chatgpt_independent_review: REVISE — Reading the encoded part/staff layout is easy; *supporting only* one pitched two-staff part is a product restriction, not evidence other arrangements cannot be analysed. Many useful beginner one-staff pieces, solo-piano reductions encoded in two parts, lead sheets and duets would become UNKNOWN. Keep raw layout inventory for every file; support canonical two-staff scores first, but return UNSUPPORTED only for analyses that truly require that layout. Music21 PartStaff is not guaranteed to appear as two Score.parts for every score. Show supported-corpus coverage and losses before accepting this boundary.

reports: For each measure: position index, printed number (measure@number), implicit flag, notated length against the time signature (full, short, over-full).
definition: Notated length of a measure = the largest end time over its voices, from <duration>, <backup> and <forward> in divisions; compared with the time signature in force.
implementation: Raw walk (the same logic file_checks.py already uses for its bar check). music21 Measure.number and paddingLeft as the second reader. All later rows report locations with the printed number, so a reader or a Haiku agent can find the bar in the score.
library_and_prior_evidence: file_checks.py already flags under-full and over-full interior bars on this pipeline; the old project's raw walk did the same.
pitfalls: Printed numbers repeated or with suffixes ('12a'), multi-bar rests, first and second endings sharing numbers, cue-size notes counted into the length.
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: 4/4 bar of four quarters -> full. Fail: 4/4 bar with three quarters and no rest -> short. Fool: a bar whose second voice has a <forward> instead of rests -> full (largest voice end), not short.
used_for: Locations in every row; anacrusis (E10); excerpts handed to Haiku agents; step 4 generator output check
why_easy: Arithmetic over durations already implemented and tested in file_checks.py.
chatgpt_independent_review: REVISE — Keep both stable measure index and printed number (including suffixes) because repeated numbers/first and second endings are not unique. Time cursors must be tracked separately for backup/forward and voices with changed divisions; maximum end time is *elapsed encoded extent*, not proof of a metrically complete, well-rested bar. Report explicit rests versus unfilled voice gaps separately; distinguish pickup, final short measure, cadenza and corrupted bars. Good reusable foundation, but the stated forward-only fool test cannot certify editorial completeness.

fact: Clefs and clef changes, per staff
reports: Starting clef of each staff (sign, line, octave change); every change as (bar, staff, from, to, inside the bar or at its start); count of changes per staff.
definition: A change is a <clef number=staff> whose sign, line or octave change differs from the clef in force on that staff. A clef equal to the one in force (restated at a system break) is not a change.
implementation: Raw walk of <attributes><clef> including attributes in the middle of a measure; a clef without a number attribute applies to staff 1. music21 clef.Clef objects per PartStaff as the second reader.
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: raw walk validated (clef changes in 145 PDMX ids, 96 inside a bar; same-clef restatements in 50 files not counted). The old app detector read staff 2 as bass and never read the clef, which failed on clef changes. music21 ran on corpus scores: staff 2 of Clara Schumann Op. 1 No. 1 has 14 bass, 7 treble and 1 treble-8va clef objects.
pitfalls: Restated clefs; cue clefs; treble-8va or bass-8vb clefs (octave change); a staff that starts in the 'wrong' clef (both staves treble).
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: corpus Maple Leaf Rag -> clef changes on staff 2 at bars 9 and 13 (as music21 reads it). Fail: a file with only the opening clefs -> 0. Fool: the same treble clef restated at every system -> 0 changes.
in_our_files: 348 of 842 files have more than two <clef> elements (includes restatements, so an upper bound)
used_for: A.1 (both clefs), 6.7 (clef changes in reading), E05 ledger lines (needs the clef in force), step 4 generator check
why_easy: Direct read; the only rule is 'changed from the clef in force'.
chatgpt_independent_review: ACCEPT WITH EDGE TEST — Compare sign, line and clef-octave-change at actual in-measure position; preserve the staff clef state from prior measures. No-number means the score-part default, usually staff 1, but check multi-clef attributes; track initial clefs separately from changes. Test same-clef restatement, one-staff two-hand display, mid-bar change and 8va clefs. E01 already filters many layouts, so do not conflate these with hand ownership.

reports: Each span: staff, kind and size, first and last bar, notes inside; spans not closed are listed as UNCLOSED with their start.
definition: <octave-shift type='up|down|stop' size='8|15' number='n'> pairs, matched by number within a staff. Notes inside a span are those between start and stop in that staff.
implementation: Raw walk; music21 spanner.Ottava as the second reader. In our files music21 imports the notes under an ottava at sounding pitch (Ottava.transposing is False); our probe on 4 candidate files found the same number of spans as the raw <octave-shift> starts in all 4.
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: own span reading agreed with music21 on 81 of 93 files (exclusive stop); unclosed spans (3 in Malagueña), empty spans and '8va cont.' words occur. Never compared with a printed page.
pitfalls: Unclosed or empty spans; '8va' written only as <words> (no span); whether the stop note is inside the span (exclusive vs inclusive).
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: an 8va over bars 5-6 of staff 1 -> one span, bars 5-6. Fail: no <octave-shift> -> none. Fool: '8va' typed as <words> with no <octave-shift> -> no span; listed under 'ottava words' only.
used_for: A.1 (a passage marked 8va), 7.8 (8va in reading), E05 (written position under an 8va)
why_easy: Direct read; library and raw reader agreed on our sample.
chatgpt_independent_review: REVISE — The MusicXML octave-shift type is from *printed* pitch to sounding pitch: a conventional 8va is a `down` shift in the element. Do not interpret `up` as sounding-up. `number` also scopes paired spanners; include `continue`, `<offset>`, and stop boundary ordering, preserving unclosed spans as UNKNOWN. Report encoded pitch and displayed pitch separately. Four sample matches support parsing, not direction/edge correctness. This is a high-impact prerequisite for E05 and E33.

reports: Per staff: notes by number of ledger lines needed (0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, more than 5), above and below; the bars of notes with 1-2 and 3+ ledger lines.
definition: Written staff position from the clef in force and the written pitch (sounding pitch moved back by any ottava in force, E04). Ledger lines needed = how many lines beyond the five staff lines the note sits on or past: middle C in treble = 1 below; A5 in treble = 1 above; C6 in treble = 2 above; middle C in bass = 1 above; E2 in bass = 1 below.
implementation: music21: diatonicNoteNum of the written pitch against clef.lowestLine (treble 31, bass 19): below = (lowestLine - d) // 2 when d < lowestLine, above = (d - topLine) // 2 when d > topLine, with topLine = lowestLine + 8 (checked by hand: treble D4 0, C4 1, B3 1, A3 2; G5 0, A5 1, B5 1, C6 2; bass E2 1, C4 1). Each note of a chord counted; grace notes counted separately. Replaces rung_pieces.py's pitch-range proxy for B.1 and 1.1.
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: own staff-position geometry validated on named pieces (Satie, Silent Night, We Three Kings); 6 or more ledger lines happen in 97 real files, many where an 8va mark was lost in transcription. The research agent checked a 3-line formula on 4 hand cases (C4 treble 1, A5 treble 1, C4 bass 1, E2 bass 1).
pitfalls: A lost 8va gives absurd counts: more than 5 is reported as 'possible missing 8va', not as a reading demand; cross-staff notes use the clef of the staff they are written on; the off-by-one between notes on a ledger line and in the space beyond it (the formula's main risk).
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: C4 treble 1 below; B3 treble 1 below (space under the first ledger line); D4 treble 0; A5 treble 1 above; B5 treble 1 above; C6 treble 2; E2 bass 1 below; C4 bass 1 above. Fail: notes inside the staff -> 0. Fool: written D6 under an 8va (sounding D7) -> 2 ledger lines, not 5.
used_for: B.1 (to two ledger lines), 1.1 (ledger lines above and below), reading difficulty, step 4 generator check (no note beyond the ledger lines a level allows)
why_easy: Small formula from two library values; the hand-made cases above pin every boundary.
chatgpt_independent_review: REVISE — Validate diatonic ledger-line arithmetic under both clefs and actual octave-shifts. Critical distinction: spaces beyond the staff count the number of ledger lines *passed*, not automatically one more (their examples look correct but require signed off-by-one cases). Treat high ledger counts as data, with a separate possible-8va warning rather than hiding valid difficult notes. Base on displayed note spelling and active clef, never MIDI-only spelling; staff number is not hand.

reports: Fifths (and mode when written) at the start and at each change, with bar and staff; number of changes.
definition: <key><fifths> (and <mode>) per staff (number attribute) or for all staves; a change is a value different from the one in force. Non-traditional keys (<key-step>/<key-alter>) are reported as such.
implementation: Raw walk; music21 key.KeySignature as the second reader (some files give the subclass key.Key, so test with isinstance).
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: validated (Beethoven Symphony 7 four changes; key changes in 55 PDMX ids). The old app detector kept only the first key. music21 on corpus Maple Leaf Rag: -4, -5, -4 at bars 0, 51, 68.
pitfalls: Signatures restated at system breaks; cancellation naturals; per-staff keys; the written mode is often missing, so the mode is never inferred here.
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: Maple Leaf Rag -> -4 (bar 0), -5 (bar 51), -4 (bar 68). Fail: a C major file with one signature -> one entry, 0 changes. Fool: G major restated at every system -> 0 changes.
used_for: B.4, 1.12 and the scale rungs' keys (which keys a piece is in), level fit (key signature size), step 4 generator check (requested key = written key)
why_easy: Direct read; library agreed on the corpus test.
chatgpt_independent_review: ACCEPT WITH EDGE TEST — Raw fifths and mode/key-step/alter plus location are explicit. Do not collapse nontraditional signatures to zero or infer the sounding tonic from them. Verify the `number` attribute for per-staff key and application at in-measure changes, mode absent, cancellation/naturals, and opening written key only. A printed key signature is a reading demand, not proof any changed degree occurs (E08 covers that).

fact: Accidentals as encoded in the file
reports: Per staff: count of <accidental> elements by kind (sharp, flat, natural, double sharp, double flat), how many are cautionary or editorial; accidentals per 100 notes; bars with the most.
definition: Only the file's own <accidental> elements: what the file says is printed. Whether a given renderer would draw an accidental is NOT computed (that is the hard part; see pitfalls).
implementation: Raw walk of <note><accidental> with its cautionary, editorial and parentheses attributes.
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: a model of which accidentals are displayed was wrong on 8,543 of 76,813 file-accidental notes (11.1%) against OpenSheetMusicDisplay's render, so the display layer is out of this batch. music21 raised 'incorrect accidental' on one old file (Mozart K. 545 alt). music21 Pitch.accidental.displayStatus exists but reading it as 'printed' is unverified.
pitfalls: Exporters that omit <accidental> for printed accidentals or add redundant ones; the count is the file's claim, not the page.
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: bar with F-sharp then F-natural, both with <accidental> -> 1 sharp, 1 natural. Fail: a C major scale -> 0. Fool: an F-sharp tied over the barline with no <accidental> on the second note -> counted once (as encoded).
in_our_files: all files (element counts not yet taken)
used_for: A.5 (sharps and flats), 1.1 (occasional accidentals), reading difficulty (accidental rate, one of Sébastien et al.'s seven criteria), step 4 generator check
why_easy: Direct read once the display question is left out.
chatgpt_independent_review: ACCEPT AS NARROW FACT — Count explicit `<accidental>` tokens by printed type and position; distinguish this carefully from the effective altered sounding pitch and from the renderer’s displayed accidentals. MusicXML allows cautionary/editorial/parentheses markers, and accidentals may also be attached to grace/cue notes; record these flags. Deliberately returning zero for an implied but unencoded natural is right for this *encoded* fact, not evidence the reader sees none.

fact: Notes the key signature actually alters
reports: For each key-signature span: which of the signature's altered letters occur with the signature's alteration, and how often.
definition: A note counts when its step is one the signature alters and its alter equals the signature's alter for that step (e.g. F-sharp under one sharp). Notes carrying a different alter (an F-natural) do not count.
implementation: music21 KeySignature.accidentalByStep(step) compared with each note's pitch.accidental alter, per key span from E06; or the same from raw <step>/<alter>.
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: implemented in the app detector (keySignature, detect.ts line 532) but measured only through its failing display model. music21 alteredPitches ran on Maple Leaf Rag (B-flat, E-flat, A-flat, D-flat); the per-note comparison was not run.
pitfalls: Non-traditional keys; a signature with no affected notes (e.g. a G major piece with no F at all) is a real result, not an error.
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: G major melody with F-sharps -> F-sharp counted. Fail: G major piece without any F -> 0 (signature not exercised). Fool: an F-natural with an explicit natural in G major -> not counted.
used_for: B.4 and 1.12 (key signatures met in pieces), step 4 generator check (an exercise in G that uses F-sharp)
why_easy: One comparison per note from library values.
chatgpt_independent_review: REVISE — The signature-altered pitch count is useful, but written `<alter>` can be omitted on notes that sound under a current key (depending on export). Resolve effective pitch from key signature and explicit accidental context rather than assuming every F-sharp has `<alter>1</alter>`; verify the input convention empirically first. A single chromatic natural on an F must not count. Compare signature state over mid-piece changes and separate changed-note counts from simply having the signature.

fact: Time signatures, changes and metre class
reports: Each signature with its bar; number of changes; class of each: simple (2, 3, 4 beats), compound (numerator 6, 9 or 12 over 4, 8 or 16), irregular (5, 7, 11 and others, and composite numerators like 3+2); 'no time signature' when absent.
definition: A change is a signature different from the one in force. Class from the numerator and denominator only, by the rule above (6/4 is compound duple; 3/8 is simple triple). Grouping of irregular metres (2+3 or 3+2) is not decided unless the numerator is written as a sum.
implementation: Raw <time><beats>/<beat-type> (with <senza-misura> and symbol attributes); music21 meter.TimeSignature.classification as the second reader.
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: music21 and partitura plain reads equal the raw reader on all 187 changes in 49 items. Gnossienne No. 1 has no <time>; partitura returns an empty list. Old detector problems were in classing a change as a device or pickup, not in reading it.
pitfalls: Restatements; a pickup written as its own short signature at the start (reported as 'possible pickup signature'); cadenza bars; cut and common time symbols (read the numbers, keep the symbol).
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: 6/8 -> compound; 3/4 then 2/4 at bar 9 -> 1 change. Fail: 4/4 throughout -> 0 changes, simple. Fool: 4/4 restated at bar 17 -> 0 changes; 3/8 -> simple, not compound.
used_for: A.3 (2/4), B.2 (a change of time signature), 1.4 (6/8), 3.3 (12/8 and changing metres), 6.7 (9/8, 5/8, 5/4), 7.8 (7/8, 7/4), step 4 generator check
why_easy: Direct read; two libraries matched the raw reader on every change tested.
chatgpt_independent_review: REVISE — Record actual `<beats>` (including additive strings) and `<beat-type>` first. The division into simple/compound is a conventional interpretation, not always determined by integer numerator/denominator alone; 6/4 can be subdivided in multiple ways. Preserve ambiguous/alternating/senza-misura cases and beaming/grouping evidence rather than asserting an unequivocal beat unit. 3/8 not compound by itself is a useful fix. Tests need a 6/4 with 3+3 vs 2+2+2 grouping and an additive meter.

reports: Whether the first bar is shorter than the signature, its length, the implicit flag, and the last bar's length (a classical pickup is often balanced by a short last bar).
definition: First measure's notated length (E02) less than the time signature's length, or measure@implicit='yes'. Both lengths are reported; nothing else is decided.
implementation: From E02. music21 Measure.paddingLeft as the second reader (corpus Maple Leaf Rag bar 0: paddingLeft 1.5, duration 0.5 of 2.0).
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: validated on 5 named items (Away in a Manger one quarter of 3/4; Alexander's Ragtime Band 2 of 4; Für Elise one eighth of 3/8; two full-bar starts).
pitfalls: A first bar that is short only because a rest was omitted looks like a pickup; the implicit flag is reported so the two cases can be told apart where the file sets it.
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: Away in a Manger (shortlist file 002) -> 1 quarter of 3. Fail: a piece starting on a full bar -> no pickup. Fool: first bar with one voice full and the other missing its rest -> full (largest voice).
used_for: A.3 (the upbeat), reading rungs, step 4 generator check
why_easy: Comes free from E02.
chatgpt_independent_review: REVISE — A short first bar is a *pickup candidate*, not always a real anacrusis; corrupt/incomplete transcription and cadenza can mimic it. Conversely `<measure implicit="yes">` may be exporter metadata, not a trustworthy pickup by itself. Report both independent observations; establish actual pickup when they agree or score context supports it. Include displaced pickup time for offset-based detectors and a last-bar complement check when present, without inventing one as a hard rule.

fact: Note and rest values, dots and ties, per staff
reports: Per staff: counts of notes and of rests by written type (whole to 32nd and shorter), dotted and double-dotted counts, tie chains (count, how many cross a barline), the shortest written value, and bars where the written type disagrees with the duration.
definition: Written <type> and <dot> of each non-grace, non-cue note and rest; a tie chain is a run of notes linked by <tie type='start'/'stop'> (two tied notes are one chain, two written notes).
implementation: Raw walk; music21 duration.type and dots as the second reader; ties from <tie> (sound) with <tied> (notation) as a check.
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: values validated over 2,020 files; every value shorter than a 128th sat in a bar that also carries a quantisation ratio (a PDMX re-export artefact); cue-size notes kept in 26 files. music21 and partitura agreed on tie starts in a corpus file (4 and 4).
pitfalls: Notes without <type> (derive from duration and report); cue notes; re-export artefacts with odd values (reported, not used for difficulty); grace notes are counted in E14, not here.
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: bar of four eighths -> 4 eighths. Fail: bar of half notes -> no eighths. Fool: a quarter tied to an eighth -> one quarter, one eighth, one tie chain; not a dotted quarter.
used_for: A.3 (rests, eighths), B.2 (eighth patterns), 2.4 (sixteenths), level fit (no sixteenths at B), difficulty (shortest value, share of short values), step 4 generator check
why_easy: Direct read; replaces the duration counting in rung_pieces.py with a tested one.
chatgpt_independent_review: REVISE — Printed duration `<type>/<dot>` and performed/encoded `<duration>` are different facts; keep both. MusicXML uses both `<tie>` playback and `<notations><tied>` engraving, which can disagree; do not rely on only `<tie>`. Tuplets, chords, rests, cross-bar chains and rearticulated same-pitch notes need separate treatment. The basic parsing is easy, but tie-chain reconstruction requires note identity by staff/voice/pitch and appropriate ambiguity handling.

reports: Per staff: count and bars of dotted quarter followed by an eighth, and of dotted eighth followed by a sixteenth, in simple metres.
definition: Two consecutive notes or rests in the same voice and staff: (dotted quarter, eighth) or (dotted eighth, sixteenth), in a bar whose metre class (E09) is simple. In compound time a dotted quarter is the beat, not the figure, so compound bars are excluded.
implementation: Per-voice sequence from the raw walk or music21; pairs read from E11 values.
library_and_prior_evidence: Old app detector (dottedQuarters, detect.ts line 416) counted simple time only; validated on 4 items (Für Elise 12 dotted-eighth pairs). rung_pieces.py already counts both figures without the simple-time rule.
pitfalls: The eighth before the dotted quarter (reverse figure) is a different figure and not counted; a dotted quarter tied into an eighth.
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: 4/4 bar 'dotted quarter, eighth, half' -> 1. Fail: even quarters -> 0. Fool: 6/8 bar of two dotted quarters -> 0.
used_for: B.2 (dotted quarter-eighth), 2.4 (dotted eighth-sixteenth), step 4 generator check
why_easy: A pair lookup over E11 with one metre condition.
chatgpt_independent_review: REVISE — Report dotted pairs only for adjacent actual *note onsets* in one voice, and optionally corresponding rest+note rhythmic cells as a separate kind. The current definition includes rests as interchangeable with notes, which can invent the wrong pedagogical pattern. A dotted-quarter/eighth may occur in various meters, so exclude compound only if this row specifically means a simple-time teaching figure; do not suppress the underlying dotted value (E11). Test ties, dotted-quarter plus rest, and voice interleaving.

reports: Per staff: groups by ratio (3:2, 6:4, 5:4, 2:3 duplets and others), notes per group, bars.
definition: A group is a printed bracket: <tuplet type='start'> ... <tuplet type='stop'> enclosing 2 or more notes whose <time-modification> ratio is not 1. Ratios on notes with no bracket element are not counted (see evidence).
implementation: Raw walk; music21 duration.tuplets as the second reader (corpus Clara Schumann Op. 1 No. 1: music21 66 notes at 3:2; partitura 22 groups; they agree).
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: raw <time-modification> alone included re-export artefacts (77 distinct ratios, e.g. 160:107); reading only closed brackets of 2 or more notes kept 14 of 14 real figures and dropped 21 of 21 artefacts, and lost 1 of 231 3:2 groups.
pitfalls: Unclosed brackets (10 in the old catalogue); nested tuplets; files that encode triplets with ratios but no <tuplet> element (missed by this definition; reported as 'unbracketed ratios' for review).
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: three eighths under a 3:2 bracket -> one triplet group. Fail: plain eighths -> 0. Fool: a 160:107 ratio with no bracket -> 0 groups, listed under unbracketed ratios.
used_for: 1.4 (triplets), 2.4 (triplets), BL.4 (triplet licks), 6.7 (triplets in reading), difficulty (tuplet share; one of Sébastien et al.'s criteria), step 4 generator check
why_easy: Direct read with the artefact rule the old project already measured.
chatgpt_independent_review: REQUIRED CHANGE — A tuplet is not synonymous with a printed bracket. MusicXML `<time-modification>` can specify triplets with no `<notations><tuplet>` bracket, including common unbracketed triplets; the present definition would miss those. Detect tuplets from effective time modification, report ratio, count and onset coverage, and separately report bracket signs if printed. Add adversarial unbracketed, nested, incomplete and two-voice tuplets. This is a material false-negative risk for rhythm lessons.

chatgpt_ids: mark.ornament (grace part); texture.crushed-note (the grace note only)
reports: Per staff: count, slashed (acciaccatura) versus unslashed (appoggiatura), runs of consecutive grace notes and their longest length, bars.
definition: Notes with a <grace> element; slash='yes' marks the slashed kind. A run is consecutive grace notes before one main note.
implementation: Raw walk; music21 duration.isGrace as the second reader (corpus Clara Schumann Op. 1 No. 3: 39 in both music21 and partitura). Do not use partitura's note_array with grace notes included (it crashed in 1.9.0).
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: 247 real items carry <grace>; runs of 6 or more occur in Chopin files (written-out flourishes).
pitfalls: Cue-size notes that are not <grace>; long grace runs are a different thing from an ornamental grace note and are reported as runs.
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: one slashed grace before a quarter -> 1 slashed. Fail: no <grace> -> 0. Fool: small cue-size notes without <grace> -> 0.
used_for: 2.6 (grace notes), 3.4 (appoggiatura), BL.6 (crushed notes), difficulty, step 4 generator check
why_easy: Direct read; two libraries agreed on the corpus test.
chatgpt_independent_review: ACCEPT WITH EDGE TEST — `<grace>` is direct; report slash attribute, run length and which main note follows. A grace cluster can span an onset/voice boundary, so pair by part/staff/voice in score order instead of treating mere XML adjacency as musical attachment. Do not infer acciaccatura/appoggiatura stylistic execution from the slash alone. Good easy score fact.

reports: Per staff: counts by kind (trill-mark, wavy-line without a trill mark, mordent, inverted mordent, turn, inverted or delayed turn, schleifer, shake, other), bars.
definition: Children of <notations><ornaments>; <tremolo> inside ornaments is E17, not here.
implementation: Raw walk; music21 note.expressions (Trill, Mordent, InvertedMordent, Turn, ...) as the second reader (corpus Op. 1 No. 3: Turn 5, Trill 2).
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: no measured finding for ornament signs; a SMuFL glyph was once misread as a fingering. rung_pieces.py counts ornaments without kinds.
pitfalls: 'tr' typed as <words>; <other-ornament> with a SMuFL glyph (reported as other).
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: a trill mark on a half note -> 1 trill. Fail: none -> 0. Fool: 'tr' as <words> -> 0 trills, listed under text.
in_our_files: trill-mark 129 (15.3%), mordent 42 (5.0%), inverted mordent 89 (10.6%), turn 17 (2.0%) of 842
used_for: 3.4 (trill, mordent), difficulty, step 4 generator check
why_easy: Direct read.
chatgpt_independent_review: ACCEPT WITH SCOPE — Detect exact ornament element tags, position and line/spanner extent, with one count for signs and another for written-out ornament realizations (not covered here). Mark custom/unknown ornament names unknown, and do not treat the sign as proof of correct ornament execution. Test trills with wavy lines and variants of mordent/turn signs.

reports: Per staff: chords with <arpeggiate> (direction when given) and with <non-arpeggiate>, bars.
definition: <notations><arpeggiate> on any note of a chord marks that chord.
implementation: Raw walk; music21 expressions.ArpeggioMark as the second reader (ran on corpus Op. 1 No. 1: 6).
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: no finding (its 'arpeggio' rule was a broken-chord pattern, a different thing).
pitfalls: Arpeggio spanning both staves (one sign per staff in the file).
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: wavy line on a 4-note chord -> 1. Fail: plain chord -> 0. Fool: a broken chord written out in eighths -> 0 (that is a pattern, not the sign).
used_for: E37 (a wide chord marked to be rolled is not a stretch), difficulty, 8.4 performance marks
why_easy: Direct read.
chatgpt_independent_review: ACCEPT WITH GROUPING FIX — An `<arpeggiate>` sign often appears on multiple chord notes; deduplicate by event/group number, staff and onset to avoid counting one rolled chord three times. Preserve direction and `<non-arpeggiate>` indications as distinct facts, with cross-staff grouping possible. The sign requests a spread, but E36 same-onset notes do not cease being a notated chord.

reports: Per staff: single-note and two-note tremolos with number of strokes, bars.
definition: <ornaments><tremolo type='single|start|stop|unmeasured'>; the text value is the number of strokes.
implementation: Raw walk; music21 expressions.Tremolo as the second reader (ran on corpus Op. 1 No. 4: 24).
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: read through partitura ornaments; no measured count.
pitfalls: Measured repeated notes written out (that is E40's repeated notes, not a tremolo sign).
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: three-stroke tremolo on a half note -> 1 single, 3 strokes. Fail: none -> 0. Fool: written-out 32nd repetitions -> 0.
used_for: BL.6 (tremolo), difficulty
why_easy: Direct read.
chatgpt_independent_review: ACCEPT WITH EDGE TEST — Report `<tremolo>` strokes and type; pair two-note start/stop across notes and distinguish single-note measured repetitions from two-note alternations. Not all strokes imply an unmeasured trill-like performance; keep printed value and style separate. Include unpaired start, one-note tremolo, two-note tremolo and tremolo versus beams.

reports: Per staff: glissando and slide spans with start and end notes, bars; 'gliss.' words listed separately.
definition: <notations><glissando> and <slide> start/stop pairs.
implementation: Raw walk; music21 spanner.Glissando as the second reader (only tested on a constructed object; no corpus piano file has one).
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: no finding.
pitfalls: 'gliss.' typed as words with no span; a span with no stop.
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: a glissando from C4 to C6 -> 1 span. Fail: none -> 0. Fool: 'gliss.' as words only -> 0 spans, listed as text.
used_for: 3.4 (glissando)
why_easy: Direct read; rare, so low value.
chatgpt_independent_review: ACCEPT WITH EDGE TEST — Match glissando and slide start/stop by number and kind, with staff and in-measure time. Prefer a source-location + intended target rather than assuming paired notes are always in one staff. A written text "gliss." with no MusicXML spanner stays text/unclassified; distinguish encoded black-key/white-key instruction if available.

reports: Fermatas on notes, rests and barlines, with bar and staff.
definition: <notations><fermata> on a note or rest, and <barline><fermata>.
implementation: Raw walk; music21 expressions.Fermata as the second reader (ran on corpus Schoenberg Op. 19/2: 2).
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: read through partitura; no measured count.
pitfalls: The same fermata written on both staves (count per staff and per time position).
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: fermata on the final chord -> 1. Fail: none -> 0. Fool: fermata on both staves at the same beat -> 1 time position, 2 marks.
used_for: A.6 (fermata), tempo-change list (E26)
why_easy: Direct read.
chatgpt_independent_review: ACCEPT — Direct token extraction from notes, rests and barlines is straightforward. Report shape (`upright`/`inverted` where encoded) and position; not duration in seconds. The same sign may attach to several notes in a chord, so distinguish mark-token count and musical-pause location. Include repeat/end-barline fermata and chords.

reports: Each mark (pppp to ffff, mp, mf, sf, sfz, sffz, fz, fp, rf, rfz, other) with bar and staff; the set of levels used; softest and loudest; time positions where the two staves have different dynamics.
definition: Children of <direction><direction-type><dynamics> (staff from the direction's <staff>) and of <notations><dynamics>. Words such as 'dolce' or 'cresc.' are not dynamics.
implementation: Raw walk; music21 dynamics.Dynamic as the second reader (corpus Op. 1 No. 1: mf 3, f 3, p 1). Do not use partitura for this: it classed the word 'calando' as a dynamic.
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: sf, sfz and fz counts read through partitura equalled the raw counts (Moonlight III 49, Hall of the Mountain King 39).
pitfalls: Dynamics typed as words ('p dolce'); <other-dynamics>; a direction without a staff number (applies to staff 1).
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: p at bar 1 and f at bar 9 -> 2 marks, range p to f. Fail: none -> empty. Fool: 'dolce' words -> not a dynamic.
used_for: A.6 (loud and soft), B.8 (pp), 1.6 (mp, mf), 3.4 (sforzando), 7.4 (different dynamics in each hand), difficulty, step 4 generator check
why_easy: Direct read.
chatgpt_independent_review: REVISE — Parse structured `<dynamics>` both in directions and notations, but do not assume each is on a determinable staff: staff may be omitted, placed between staves, or spread over a group. Preserve `staff_unspecified` rather than defaulting to staff 1. Written `sfz`, `fp`, `rfz` are not directly comparable on one ppp–fff numerical scale. Separate written symbol from measured performance dynamic and from generic expressive words.

reports: Wedges (crescendo, diminuendo) with staff and bars; 'cresc.', 'dim.', 'decresc.' words listed separately with bars.
definition: <wedge type='crescendo|diminuendo|stop' number>; words matched against a closed list (cresc, crescendo, dim, diminuendo, decresc, decrescendo, with or without a full stop).
implementation: Raw walk; music21 dynamics.Crescendo and Diminuendo as the second reader (corpus Op. 1 No. 1: 2 crescendos). partitura found none on the same file, so it is not used.
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: crescendo read through partitura; diminuendo apparently missing there.
pitfalls: Unclosed wedges; a wedge on one staff meant for both.
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: a crescendo wedge over bars 3-4 -> 1. Fail: none -> 0. Fool: 'cresc.' words -> 0 wedges, 1 word.
used_for: A.6, B.8 and 1.6 (crescendo, diminuendo, hairpins), step 4 generator check
why_easy: Direct read; music21 matched on the corpus test.
chatgpt_independent_review: ACCEPT WITH EDGE TEST — Distinguish wedge spanners (numbered start/stop, `continue` where present) from crescendo/diminuendo words and retain ambiguous/unmatched text. A word is a label, not an inferred duration span unless anchored by explicit markup; do not fabricate a fade interval after "cresc.". Keep numbered overlapping hairpins, directions without staff and words like `cresc. poco a poco` as test cases.

reports: Per staff: counts by kind (staccato, staccatissimo, tenuto, detached-legato, accent, strong accent, spiccato, breath mark, other), bars.
definition: Children of <notations><articulations>.
implementation: Raw walk; music21 note.articulations as the second reader (corpus Op. 1 No. 1: staccato 12, accent 8 in music21 and partitura alike).
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: accents read through partitura (accent items 101 PDMX).
pitfalls: Articulations typed as words; a staccato on every note of a chord counted once per chord (report both).
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: four staccato quarters -> 4 staccatos. Fail: none -> 0. Fool: a 3-note chord with one staccato -> 1 chord.
used_for: A.2 (staccato), A.6 and 1.6 (accents), step 4 generator check
why_easy: Direct read; two libraries agreed.
chatgpt_independent_review: ACCEPT — Report exact articulation tags and note/staff position, with compound/articulation glyph variants retained. A `staccato` mark is a requested touch, not a proven staccato note duration in performance. Keep notations attached to multiple chord notes from being mistaken for multiple independent attacks. Add adversarial tenuto+staccato and jazz-specific tags.

reports: Per staff: number of slurs, notes under slurs (share of all notes), average notes per slur, bars; slurs that join two notes of the same pitch listed separately (likely a mis-encoded tie).
definition: <slur type='start|stop' number> paired by number within a staff and voice.
implementation: Raw walk; music21 spanner.Slur as the second reader.
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: no finding. rung_pieces.py counts music21 Slur objects in the bars used.
pitfalls: Dangling starts or stops; slurs crossing staves; same-pitch slurs.
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: a slur over four notes -> 1 slur, 4 notes. Fail: none -> 0. Fool: a 'slur' between two Cs of the same pitch -> listed as possible tie.
used_for: A.2 (legato), B.8 (phrase marks), 1.6 (slurs), step 4 generator check
why_easy: Direct read.
chatgpt_independent_review: REVISE — Slur identity is scoped by MusicXML number within the relevant part and staff context, but spanning notes may change voice; hard-keying both staff and voice can strand legitimate slurs. Capture source/target notes, number, position and ambiguity with tests for overlapping slurs and cross-voice starts/stops. Do not equate slur to successful legato, phrasing or a note-by-note fingering recommendation.

reports: Pedal events (start, change, stop) with bars; pedalled spans; share of bars under pedal; sostenuto; una corda and tre corde from words.
definition: <direction-type><pedal type='start|stop|change|continue|sostenuto|resume|discontinue'>; words matched to a closed list for una corda / u.c. / tre corde / con pedale / senza pedale.
implementation: Raw walk; music21 expressions.PedalMark as the second reader. Our probe on 4 candidate files: music21 32 against 33 raw starts in one file, equal in the other three, so the raw count is the reference.
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: no finding. rung_pieces.py counts any object whose class name contains 'pedal' (replaced by this row).
pitfalls: 'Ped.' as words only; pedal lines with no stop; marks on staff 1 applying to the whole piano.
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: Ped. at bar 1, change at bar 2, release at bar 3 -> 1 span with 1 change. Fail: none -> 0. Fool: 'con pedale' words with no marks -> 0 events, listed as text.
used_for: A.6 (first pedal), B.8 (connected pedal), 1.6 (pedalling), 7.4 (una corda), J.5 (pedal in tunes), step 4 generator check
why_easy: Direct read.
chatgpt_independent_review: REVISE — The structured pedal events are direct, but they can be associated with the whole piano part rather than staff 1; do not invent a hand or per-staff pedal when `<staff>` is omitted. Preserve `<pedal>` type, number, line/sign, start/change/stop and encoded depth if present, plus separate closed-vocabulary text. `una corda` is soft pedal, not sustain; these must not share a generic pedal label. An absent sign does not mean pedal is inappropriate.

reports: Metronome marks (beat unit, dots, per minute, bar); <sound tempo> values (quarter notes per minute) with bars; the opening tempo word matched to a closed list (Grave to Prestissimo); a tempo map in quarter notes per minute.
definition: <metronome><beat-unit>, <beat-unit-dot>, <per-minute>; <sound tempo> is quarter notes per minute by the MusicXML definition. A dotted-quarter = 60 mark becomes 90 quarters per minute. A tempo word alone gives no number (a default number per word would be a guess).
implementation: Raw walk; music21 tempo.MetronomeMark.getQuarterBPM and metronomeMarkBoundaries as the second reader. partitura returned no tempo directions on a corpus file that has them, so it is not used.
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: validated on named items (Op. 10 No. 1 quarter = 176; Asturias has no metronome mark but <sound tempo> 144).
pitfalls: A metronome mark and a <sound tempo> that disagree (report both); per-minute ranges ('100-108'); marks that are words only.
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: quarter = 120 -> 120. Fail: no tempo at all -> UNKNOWN. Fool: dotted quarter = 60 in 6/8 -> 90 quarters per minute, not 60.
used_for: Notes per second (D01), step 4 generator check (exercise at the requested tempo)
why_easy: Direct read plus one unit conversion.
chatgpt_independent_review: REVISE — Keep three distinct observations: notated metronome mark, `<sound tempo>` playback value, and text tempo. Do not silently choose one if they disagree. Confirm MusicXML metronome ranges or metric-modulation equality are handled as nonnumeric/partial rather than parsed as a single BPM; use beat-unit dots for conversions and position before first note correctly. An opening mark after sounding notes is not opening tempo. Conditional durations in D01 must remain UNKNOWN when sound tempo looks like an exporter default.

reports: Each rit., rall., accel., a tempo, Tempo I, rubato, allargando, stringendo, meno mosso, più mosso, and swing or straight-eighths directions (words, or the <swing> element), with bar; unrecognised direction words listed unclassified.
definition: <direction-type><words> matched case-insensitively to the closed list above and its abbreviations (rit., ritard., ritardando, rall., rallentando, accel., accelerando). Anything else is listed as 'other words', never classified.
implementation: Raw walk over <words>; music21 TextExpression as the second reader (music21 does not turn these into RitardandoSpanner from XML).
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: validated on named items (Op. 9 No. 2 'poco rit.', 'a tempo'); French words ('Animez un peu') stayed unclassified.
pitfalls: Words in other languages; words split across two directions.
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: 'rit.' at bar 15, 'a tempo' at bar 17 -> 2 entries. Fail: none -> empty. Fool: 'ritmico' (a character word) -> other words, not a ritardando.
in_our_files: words present in 553 of 842 (65.7%); tempo-change share not counted yet
used_for: A.6 (ritardando), 7.8 (tempo changes in reading), J.1 and 2.4 (a swing direction in a piece), step 4 generator check
why_easy: Closed word list; unknown words are listed, not guessed.
chatgpt_independent_review: REVISE — The `reports` column promises rubato, allargando, stringendo, a tempo, Swing and straight-eighths, but the `definition` lists only rit/rall/accel variants. Make the closed vocabulary explicit and comprehensive for those promised kinds, plus parse structured `<swing>` independently. Simple substring matching must not classify `ritmico` or `accelerated` as rit/accel. Unrecognized words retain the raw text; they are not an absence of expression.

reports: Per staff: share of notes with a <fingering>, substitutions (e.g. 3-1), bars; digit-only <words> or lyrics listed separately as possible fingering.
definition: <notations><technical><fingering> (with substitution and alternate attributes).
implementation: Raw walk; music21 articulations.Fingering as the second reader. partitura keeps them on note.technical (its iter_all found none).
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: validated (Hanon 1 right hand 61 digits; Mozart K. 2 easy had 0 <fingering> but 71 digit words).
pitfalls: Fingering typed as words or lyrics; '0'; stacked chord fingerings.
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: five fingered notes -> share 5 of n. Fail: none -> 0. Fool: digits typed as lyrics -> 0 fingerings, listed as possible fingering text.
used_for: Information for lessons and Haiku agents (scale and early-position pieces: P.4, A.2, B.4, 1.2); step 4 generator check (fingering printed where the exercise promises it)
why_easy: Direct read.
chatgpt_independent_review: ACCEPT WITH EDGE TEST — Structured fingering is a reliable printed fact. Count per note and per chord rather than one digit per sounding note; distinguish substitutions and alternates. Preserve digit-only free text as an unverified possible fingering, not a match. Use for showing/choosing teaching material only: a printed finger 3 does not prove the fingering suits the learner or is actually played.

chatgpt_ids: notation.chord-symbols; harmony.rhythm and harmony.chord-vocabulary (from symbols only)
reports: Number of chord symbols, distinct symbols, kinds (major, minor, dominant 7th, other), slash basses, N.C., duplicates removed (the same symbol on both staves at the same time), symbols per bar, bars.
definition: <harmony> with <root>/<root-step>, <root-alter>, <kind>, <bass>; chord names typed as <words> are not counted here.
implementation: Raw walk; music21 harmony.ChordSymbol as the second reader for <harmony> elements only.
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: own reader and music21's <harmony> reader equal on 459 of 460 items; duplicates on two staves were common (4,984 down to 3,619 after removing them). music21's text parser misread 'Bb7' as root B, so text chord names are left out.
pitfalls: Duplicates on both staves; guitar-frame symbols; Roman-numeral or function kinds.
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: C, F, G7 over three bars -> 3 symbols, 3 distinct. Fail: none -> 0. Fool: 'Bb7' typed as words -> 0 symbols here.
used_for: B.7 (first lead sheet: a piece with chord symbols), 4.3, 5.3, J.1, J.3, PR.1 (lead sheets), step 4 generator check
why_easy: Direct read; the library agreed on 459 of 460.
chatgpt_independent_review: REVISE — Read `<harmony>` structurally; preserve root alteration, bass inversion, chord-kind modifiers and unknown kinds instead of lumping everything into major/minor/7/other where the lessons need extensions. Deduplicate only truly duplicate annotations at the same musical position and with identical content; two different chords at the same position could be conflicting evidence, not safe to merge. N.C. often has no root; do not drop it as a parser error. Separate label recognition from meaningful progression/harmonic analysis.

reports: Slash noteheads and slash measure styles, bars.
definition: <notehead>slash</notehead>; <measure-style><slash> or <beat-repeat>.
implementation: Raw walk.
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: validated (So Danço Samba 28 slashes; no measure-style slash anywhere).
pitfalls: None known beyond rarity.
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: four slash noteheads in a bar -> 4. Fail: normal noteheads -> 0. Fool: x noteheads -> 0.
used_for: Comping charts (B.7, J and PR rungs); very rare in our files
why_easy: Direct read; low value.
chatgpt_independent_review: ACCEPT WITH EDGE TEST — Differentiate slash-head individual notes, measure-style slash notation, and beat-repeat (`<beat-repeat>` is not the same as slash comping). Do not infer improvisation space merely from a slash head; it may be a percussion rhythm or stylistic notation. Verify repetitions, slash durations and unsupported mixed notation. This is an encoded chart fact, not evidence of a player’s chosen comp pattern.

fact: Repeat signs, endings and jump marks (presence only)
reports: Forward and backward repeat barlines with bars, endings with numbers and bars, D.C., D.S., Fine, Coda, Segno marks with bars.
definition: <barline><repeat direction>, <ending number type>, <segno>, <coda>, and <sound dacapo|dalsegno|fine|tocoda> plus words matched to D.C./D.S./Fine/Coda. The order in which the bars are played is NOT computed in this batch.
implementation: Raw walk; music21 bar.Repeat and spanner.RepeatBracket as the second reader.
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: reading the signs is easy; expanding them is not: on 81 disputed files music21's expander was right on 27 and partitura's on 21, while the old project's own unroller reached 80 of 81 only after a coda fix. Expansion is left for a later batch.
pitfalls: Jumps written only as words; endings without numbers.
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: a backward repeat at bar 8 with endings 1 and 2 -> listed. Fail: none -> empty. Fool: a double barline (not a repeat) -> not listed.
used_for: 1.7 (form: whether repeats exist, not what the form is), step 4 generator check; played length later
why_easy: Direct read once expansion is left out.
chatgpt_independent_review: ACCEPT WITH SCOPING FIX — Recording repeat/jump symbols without expanding playback is appropriately modest. Preserve element type, printed bar ID, bar position, number(s) and unpaired/endings malformed flags. D.C./D.S. word detection needs exact token boundaries and combinations such as al Fine/al Coda; ordinary song titles like `Coda` should not count unless their direction context supports it. Explicitly do not derive played bar count or named form from mere presence.

reports: Number of measures, number excluding a pickup, total notated length in quarter notes (repeats not expanded).
definition: Count of <measure> elements in the part; length from E02.
implementation: Raw walk; music21 measure count as the second reader.
library_and_prior_evidence: shortlist.csv and the file checks already report bars this way.
pitfalls: Multi-bar rests count as one measure each in the file (correct).
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: 16 measures -> 16. Fail: n/a. Fool: a pickup plus 16 full bars -> 17 measures, 16 excluding the pickup.
used_for: Level fit (at most 48 bars at Level B), difficulty (length; one of Sébastien et al.'s criteria), step 4 generator check
why_easy: A count.
chatgpt_independent_review: REVISE — Distinguish stored `<measure>` elements from semantic measures: a multimeasure rest may be encoded as one displayed multirest or as many measures, and repeats can change duration. The assertion that multibar rests count one measure in the file is a *raw-count* fact, not necessarily musical length. Report raw count, written quarter-duration, pickup status and uncertainty separately. The reference to `at most 48 bars at Level B` is not supported by this row; do not turn it into a curriculum threshold.

fact: Pitch range per staff, whole piece and per bar
reports: Per staff: lowest and highest sounding pitch, span in semitones; the same per bar; grace notes included and excluded.
definition: Sounding MIDI pitch of every non-cue note written on the staff (ottava already applied, E04).
implementation: music21 pitches per PartStaff, or analysis.discrete.Ambitus().getPitchSpan; partitura note_array pitch and staff fields as the second reader (corpus Op. 1 No. 1 staff 1: E-flat4 to E-flat7 in both).
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: validated (Asturias compass 31-103). Range bounds it used came from jSymbolic as kept in music21.
pitfalls: Staff is not hand: notes written on one staff and played by the other hand are counted on their staff. This row never says 'hand'.
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: right hand C4-G4 -> 7 semitones. Fail: n/a. Fool: a note under an 8va written C6 -> counted at C7.
used_for: P.4 and A.2 (five-finger range), A.1 and B.1 (reading range), difficulty (range), level fit, step 4 generator check (range limits)
why_easy: Min and max over library pitches; two libraries agreed.
chatgpt_independent_review: REVISE — Range by encoded staff is direct, but clarify whether `<pitch>` under `<octave-shift>` is already sounding: MusicXML pitch is generally performance pitch and E04 should be used to derive the *displayed* pitch, not add another octave to sounded MIDI. The E33 fool example must be tested for this exact direction or will double-shift C6 to C7. Distinguish source MIDI pitch, printed staff position and explicit octave-shift; compute range over sounding pitches without assuming staff=hand.

reports: Per staff and overall: distinct pitches, distinct pitch classes, share of notes on black keys (pitch classes 1, 3, 6, 8, 10), counting every note of every chord.
definition: Attacked notes (tie continuations not counted again); grace notes excluded.
implementation: music21 or partitura pitches; own one-line count.
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: validated (G-flat arpeggio share 1.0; G-flat five-finger 0.778). The research agent's quick share left chord notes out; this definition includes them.
pitfalls: Enharmonic spelling does not matter here (C-flat is a white key).
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: C major scale -> 0 black. Fail: n/a. Fool: a chord C-E-flat-G -> 1 of 3 black, counted inside the chord.
used_for: P.1 (black-key groups), P.4 (white-key positions), difficulty, step 4 generator check
why_easy: A count.
chatgpt_independent_review: ACCEPT — Distinguish MIDI pitch, written spelling, and pitch class; black-key share is keyboard geography irrespective of enharmonic spelling. Record counting policy for grace notes, cue notes, tied continuations, simultaneous duplicate voices and rests. A key with black notes is not evidence a piece teaches black-key *groups* or particular fingerings; use the inventory as material-selection evidence, not skill certification.

reports: Per staff and overall: Shannon entropy in bits of the pitch distribution and of the pitch-class distribution.
definition: H = -sum(p log2 p) over the shares of attacked notes per pitch (or pitch class); tie continuations and grace notes excluded.
implementation: numpy over the note list (muspy has the same one-line function; adding it as a dependency is not worth it).
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: validated with an independent implementation (Hall of the Mountain King right hand 5.42; ostinato fifths 1.0).
pitfalls: Longer pieces have more varied pitches; the statistic is reported with the note count.
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: two pitches equally often -> 1.0. Fail: one pitch only -> 0. Fool: four pitches, one taking 97% -> well below 2.
used_for: Difficulty only
why_easy: A formula.
chatgpt_independent_review: ACCEPT AS DESCRIPTIVE STATISTIC — Formula is deterministic with stated attack-count policy, but its relationship to difficulty is not automatically monotonic. A small recurring chromatic figure can have low entropy yet be hard; a long slow varied piece may have high entropy yet be easy. Preserve note count, per-voice/staff policy and whether pitches or classes, and do not assign grade from this alone.

reports: Per staff: histogram of how many notes start together (1, 2, 3, 4, 5 or more), the largest, the bars with 4 or more; harmonic intervals of two-note attacks (in semitones).
definition: Notes on the same staff with the same onset, across all written voices; grace notes and tie continuations excluded. The largest chord within one written voice is reported too (the two differed on 23 of the 109 shortlist files).
implementation: Group the note list by (staff, onset); music21 chord.Chord size per voice as the second view.
library_and_prior_evidence: ChatGPT's shortlist review used the per-staff definition; my recount per voice agreed on bars, notes and grace notes on all 109 files, and differed on the largest chord on 23 because of the definition.
pitfalls: Two voices on one staff may be split between the hands; stacks of 7 or more on one staff usually mean duplicated voices (Clair de lune had 8 in one voice), reported as 'possible encoding fault'.
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: a C-E-G chord -> one 3-note attack. Fail: single notes -> all 1. Fool: two voices on staff 1 starting a 2-note chord and a single note together -> 3 per staff, 2 per voice.
used_for: Level fit (at most 3-note chords at Level B), B.5 (triads in pieces), difficulty (polyphony; one of Sébastien et al.'s criteria), encoding-fault flag, step 4 generator check
why_easy: A group-by over the note list.
chatgpt_independent_review: REVISE — Simultaneous onset grouping over one staff is measurable; merging *written voices* can create a spurious single-hand chord if those voices belong to different hands or are duplicated. Preserve both by-staff and by-voice histograms plus ambiguity flags; avoid interpreting staff-wide stacks as playable single-hand attacks. Deduplicate same-pitch unison doublings with an explicit policy; identify chord size per real onset versus held harmonies.

fact: Span of notes struck together, per staff
reports: Per staff: largest and median span in semitones of notes starting together; bars with spans over 12 and over 14; whether the chord carries an arpeggio sign (E16).
definition: Highest minus lowest pitch in each per-staff attack from E36.
implementation: From E36.
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: a reach flag over 16 semitones was validated as a flag only (43 PDMX files flagged).
pitfalls: A span on one staff may be shared between hands; a rolled chord is not a stretch; neither is decided here, only reported.
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: C4-C5 -> 12. Fail: single notes -> 0. Fool: a 10th marked with an arpeggio sign -> 16 reported with the arpeggio flag.
used_for: Difficulty (stretch), playability flags, level fit
why_easy: Subtraction over E36.
chatgpt_independent_review: ACCEPT WITH SCOPE — `highest - lowest` per encoded same-onset staff cluster is simple, but label it vertical *pitch span*, not required physical hand stretch. A rolled chord may need less simultaneous reach; duplicated voices and opposite-hand notes on one staff also inflate span. Keep the roll flag from E16 and show register context. Teacher judgment or fingering data determines whether it is safely reachable.

reports: Per staff: attacks whose lowest and highest notes are exactly 12 semitones apart (with at most one note between), the longest run of consecutive octave attacks, bars.
definition: From E36 attacks: highest - lowest = 12 and at most 3 notes.
implementation: From E36 (music21 hasAnyRepeatedDiatonicNote returned 0 on a corpus file that has octaves, so it is not used).
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: no finding.
pitfalls: Broken octaves (alternating) are a pattern, not this row.
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: C3+C4 -> octave. Fail: C3+G3 -> not. Fool: C3+E3+G3+C4 (4 notes) -> not an octave attack.
used_for: Difficulty (octave passages), RG.4 and BL.6 (octave textures)
why_easy: Arithmetic over E36.
chatgpt_independent_review: REVISE — Highest-minus-lowest = 12 and at most three notes is an octave-span cluster, not necessarily an octave played as such: C-E-C contains a complete triadic chord with octave doubling. Report `contains an octave pair`, `pure octave dyad`, and `octave doubling within chord` separately if needed. Do not claim repeated or broken octaves from this row. A two-note C3/C4 test is unambiguous.

fact: Melodic leaps and jumps, per staff
reports: Per staff: histogram of intervals in semitones between consecutive attacks, largest leap, and the count of jumps over 12 semitones made in less than 2 beats.
definition: The outer line of each staff by convention: the top note of each attack on staff 1 and the bottom note on staff 2; interval = pitch difference between consecutive attacks of that line. Also per written voice where a staff has more than one voice. The jump count follows Sébastien et al. (2012): over 12 semitones within 2 beats.
implementation: From the note list sorted by onset per staff.
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: no measured finding (the app detector counted steps, skips and leaps on chord tops and bottoms). music21 melodicIntervals and its jSymbolic interval features mix both staves, so per-staff is our own.
pitfalls: With two voices on a staff, the top line jumps between voices; the per-voice figure is reported beside it. This is a statistic, not a melody.
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: C4-D4-E4 -> two steps of 2. Fail: one repeated note -> 0. Fool: an Alberti figure on staff 2 -> the bottom line stays put on repeated low notes; the jumps come from the upper notes only in the per-voice figure.
used_for: A.1 (intervals to the 5th), B.1 (intervals to the octave), difficulty (hand displacement), step 4 generator check (interval limits)
why_easy: Differences over a sorted list; the convention is stated, not inferred.
chatgpt_independent_review: REVISE — Calling the chosen upper/lower outer note line `melodic` can mislead badly in multi-voice textures; it can jump between unrelated voices as chords turn over. Keep named `staff outer-edge displacement` distinct from actual per-voice melodic intervals, noting when voice assignments are unreliable. Measure interval direction, written generic size and elapsed time; jump >12 semitones within 2 beats is an operational statistic, not a universal definition of difficulty or a real position shift.

fact: Repeated notes and runs of equal values
reports: Per staff and voice: longest run of the same pitch struck again and again; longest run of consecutive attacks with the same written value (count, value, bars).
definition: Runs inside one written voice, broken by a rest, a tie or a different value.
implementation: From the per-voice note list.
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: validated (Asturias right hand repeated-note run 96; Hanon 20 run of 241 sixteenths).
pitfalls: Voices badly separated in the file give short runs.
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: 16 sixteenths in a row -> run 16. Fail: alternating values -> 1. Fool: 8 sixteenths, an eighth rest, 8 sixteenths -> two runs of 8, not 16.
used_for: 1.13, 2.11, 3.10 (Hanon-type even streams), difficulty (endurance), step 4 generator check
why_easy: Run-length count.
chatgpt_independent_review: REVISE — This combines two distinct counters: consecutive repeated *pitches* and uninterrupted equal-*duration* streams. Supply separate outputs and tests; Hanon-style sixteenth run may change pitch at every note, while repeated-note studies may change values. Tied continuations should merge, but a rest breaks both runs. Different voice labels within a staff can be exporter artefacts, so mark uncertain long-run claims rather than treating them as canonical.

reports: Per staff: number of distinct <voice> numbers per bar; bars with 2 or more voices.
definition: The file's own <voice> numbers on each staff. Not musical independence and not an estimate.
implementation: Raw walk; music21 Measure.voices as the second reader. partitura estimate_voices is NOT used (an estimate across staves; it raised RecursionError on a corpus file).
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: voice collisions found in a few files; no count.
pitfalls: Exporters create voices for single notes (a voice with one note in one bar).
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: a bar with voices 1 and 2 on staff 1 -> 2. Fail: one voice -> 1. Fool: voice 2 holding only rests -> reported, with notes-in-voice count 0.
used_for: Excerpts for readers (voices listed separately, as ref_check.py already does), 7.4 (a pointer to contrapuntal pieces, not a judgment), difficulty (polyphony)
why_easy: Direct read.
chatgpt_independent_review: ACCEPT — Explicit voice labels per staff are straightforward. Separate declared voice count, voices with sounded notes, and apparent independent *musical* voices; a voice composed entirely of rests must not raise contrapuntal complexity. Some scores omit `<voice>` for every note, so specify default unlabelled voice; watch repeated voice numbers used on both staves and per-measure reassignment.

fact: Attack rate per staff and the ratio between staves
reports: Per bar and overall: attacks per beat on each staff; the ratio; share of beats with an attack on either staff.
definition: Attacks = distinct onsets of non-grace notes per staff; beat from the time signature in force.
implementation: From the note list.
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: beat-onset share validated on one item (Hanon 61 of 62).
pitfalls: Staff is not hand (the old project found the staff rule disagreeing with a second reader on 3.3% of notes in a 33-item sample, and wrong on 41.5% of notes under printed hand words); rows say 'staff'.
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: eighths over half notes in 4/4 -> 2 and 0.5 per beat. Fail: n/a. Fool: a chord counts as one attack, not three.
used_for: A.4 (hands together), 1.5 (busy left hand under a melody), difficulty (coordination)
why_easy: Counting onsets.
chatgpt_independent_review: REVISE — Define denominator carefully: quarter-note units versus felt beats change in 6/8, 9/8 and additive meters. Provide attacks per quarter-length and per explicitly chosen beat separately. Ratio is undefined if one staff has zero attacks; do not report infinity as coordination difficulty. Include changing metre and no-note bars. Importantly these are staff rates; the README’s staff ≠ hand caveat must propagate to every learner claim.

reports: Share of attack times where both staves attack together; share of bars where both staves sound at some point.
definition: Attack times on staff 1 and staff 2 compared exactly (same onset).
implementation: Set intersection over onset times per staff.
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: handsTogether detector exists (detect.ts line 611); no measured finding.
pitfalls: As E42 (staff, not hand).
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: melody over a held chord each bar -> low shared share, both staves sound in every bar. Fail: right hand alone -> 0. Fool: a staff-2 note tied over the barline -> sounds but does not attack.
used_for: A.4 (hands together), difficulty (coordination), step 4 generator check
why_easy: Set intersection.
chatgpt_independent_review: ACCEPT WITH NORMALIZATION FIX — Attack-set intersection is exact over notation offsets, but `share` needs a declared denominator (union of distinct attacks is easy to interpret). Return both whole-piece and per-bar shares, distinguish both-staves-sounding overlap from both-staves-attacking-simultaneously, and handle no attacks as n/a. A tie crossing a boundary must not count as a fresh attack. This is a coordination descriptor, not a measure of mastery.

reports: Bars where both staves have notes but never sound at the same moment; longest run of such bars; hand-off count.
definition: Within a bar: the sounding intervals (onset to onset + duration, ties merged) of staff 1 and staff 2 never overlap, and both staves have notes.
implementation: Interval overlap test per bar.
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: no finding.
pitfalls: Pedal makes notes overlap in sound; this row uses written durations only.
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: right hand bars 1-2, left hand bars 3-4 on separate beats -> turn-taking. Fail: melody over chords -> no. Fool: left hand note held under the right hand's entry -> overlap, so not turn-taking.
used_for: P.5 and A.4 (pieces where hands alternate before playing together)
why_easy: Interval overlap.
chatgpt_independent_review: REQUIRED CHANGE TO TEST — Definition requires *both staves sounding within the same bar* and zero overlap. But the proposed pass example `right hand bars 1–2; left hand bars 3–4` has one staff alone in each bar, and therefore must FAIL by the definition. Replace with alternating notes inside one bar, or broaden the definition to allow successive-bar handoffs as a separately named characteristic. Count overlap by intervals, not just shared attacks; label staves rather than hands.

fact: One staff holding while the other moves
reports: Spans where a note or chord on one staff sounds for at least one beat (ties merged) while the other staff has 2 or more attacks; count, total beats, bars, which staff holds.
definition: Exact intervals from written durations; 'at least one beat' from the time signature in force.
implementation: Interval test over the note lists.
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: no finding.
pitfalls: As E42 (staff, not hand); pedal ignored.
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: a whole-note chord on staff 2 under four quarters on staff 1 -> one span of 4 beats. Fail: both staves in quarters together -> none. Fool: staff 2 repeating the same chord in quarters -> no hold (re-struck).
used_for: A.4 and 1.5 (held accompaniment under a moving melody), 2.5 (a setting for voicing practice; voicing itself is not detected)
why_easy: Interval test.
chatgpt_independent_review: ACCEPT WITH TIMING CLARITY — A sustained note/chord with at least two attacks on the other staff is observable from encoded durations; the exact elapsed metric should be defined in quarter lengths or time-signature-specific beat units. Distinguish one sustained voice from multiple notes staggered in a chord; omit pedal-induced sustain unless encoded. Intended balance/voicing is not detectable from the score event count alone.

reports: Per staff-bar: notes, accidentals (E07), ledger-line notes (E05); the median and the densest bars.
definition: Counts from E05, E07 and E11 per bar and staff.
implementation: Combines earlier rows.
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: uncertain (La Campanella at most 34 notes on one staff-bar) because it used the failing display model for accidentals; E07 avoids that.
pitfalls: Density is not difficulty by itself (repetition makes dense bars easy to read).
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: a bar with 8 notes and 2 accidentals -> 8 and 2. Fail: an empty bar -> 0. Fool: a whole-bar rest in one staff -> 0 notes on that staff.
used_for: Choosing excerpts for the reading rungs (B.12, 1.11, 2.10, 3.9, 4.7, 5.7, 6.7, 7.8, 8.8), difficulty
why_easy: Sums of earlier rows.
chatgpt_independent_review: ACCEPT AS MEASURE — The chosen note, accidentals-as-encoded, and ledger-count features are simple and useful for locating busy passages, but report them separately plus a size-normalized value when compared across meters. Literal `E07` encoded accidentals may undercount what an engraving renderer displays. Density is not a calibrated sight-reading grade; repetition, rhythm and polyphony matter. Keep this as input evidence for lesson excerpt selection.

fact: Notes per second at the marked tempo
reports: Per staff and both together: attacks per second and notes per second (chord notes each counted), over the whole piece and its densest 4 bars, at the tempo map from E25; repeats not expanded.
definition: Quarter-note positions converted to seconds with the tempo map; no tempo -> UNKNOWN (no default tempo is assumed). For 8notes songs the tempo 8notes lists can be used, marked as from 8notes (the owner allowed 8notes tempos earlier).
implementation: music21 secondsMap or own conversion from E25; partitura not used for tempo.
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: validated (Hanon 20 3.89 notes a second at quarter = 60; Op. 10 No. 1 right hand 11.32 at 176). Playing speed is the first of Sébastien et al.'s seven criteria.
pitfalls: The marked tempo may be an editor's or a MIDI export's default (a <sound tempo> of exactly 120 with no metronome mark is reported as 'possible default').
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: sixteenths at quarter = 60 -> 4 per second. Fail: no tempo -> UNKNOWN. Fool: dotted quarter = 60 in 6/8 eighths -> 3 per second, not 2.
in_our_files: tempo known in up to 602 of 842 (71.5%) through <sound tempo>
used_for: Difficulty
why_easy: Arithmetic over E25 and the note list.
chatgpt_independent_review: REVISE — The computation is arithmetic *only once tempo is reliable*. Distinguish tempo from `<sound tempo>` exporter default, written metronome, borrowed 8notes tempo and UNKNOWN. Count note attacks versus sounding note density separately and handle variable tempo, metric-modulation and repeats clearly. A single tempo mark at 120 is not proof the passage is meant as 120 performance practice. Use for describing physical rate, not an objective difficulty label.

fact: Difficulty statistics measured against published levels
chatgpt_ids: difficulty.level; difficulty.reading; difficulty.rhythm; difficulty.pitch-navigation; difficulty.technique; meta.published-grade
reports: For each statistic (D01, E35 entropy, E33 range, E37 largest span, E39 jumps per bar, E36 share of chords and largest chord, E07 accidentals per 100 notes, E11 shortest value and share of sixteenths or shorter, E13 tuplet share, E14 grace notes per 100 notes, E41 voices, E32 length, E06 signature size, E09 compound or changing metre): its rank correlation with the published level; then the share of held-out files a simple combination places within one level; then a list of files whose statistics disagree with their listed level by 3 or more (mismatch alarm).
definition: Published levels from chosen.csv (135 files, checked identity) reported separately from the exam-list matches in candidates-passing.csv (395 distinct files, identity matched by title, arrangement not checked). Levels on our spine (B, 1-8). The combination is fitted on part of the files and tested on the rest (leave-one-out), and the pass mark is fixed before the run.
implementation: numpy and scipy (Spearman); a small ordinal model or nearest-neighbour median; no new dependency.
library_and_prior_evidence: Published: Ramoneda et al. 2022 (Mikrokosmos, 3 classes) report a notes-only baseline of 64±8% test accuracy and 78±6% with fingering features (read from the PDF). The old project fitted a level on its own levels (645 items) with no outside calibration; that is why published levels are the target here.
pitfalls: Exam-list matches include wrong arrangements (the 109-file review found several), so their labels are noisy; levels B-2 are mostly simple arrangements and Grades 6-8 mostly originals, so the statistics may separate styles as much as levels.
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass mark (proposal): within one level on 70% of held-out chosen.csv files. Fail: below that, the combination is not used to assign levels, only as a mismatch alarm. Fool check: shuffle the levels and rerun; the score must fall to chance.
in_our_files: 530 files with a published level (135 + 395, overlap not yet removed)
used_for: Step 3: a check on published placements (mismatch alarm); a judged level, labelled 'judged, not published', only if the pass mark is met and the owner wants it
why_easy: Statistics over rows above; the risk is in reading the result, not in the code.
chatgpt_independent_review: NOT EASY; REVISE EVALUATION — Training a difficulty model from only 135 curated labels is a calibration/validation problem, not another direct extraction. `within one level on 70%` is an arbitrary pass target without baseline, class distribution or uncertainty; a constant middle-grade prediction might achieve a surprisingly high within-one score. Leave-one-out tuning/model selection leaks information if parameters/features are chosen after seeing results. Use grouped-by-work/arrangement leakage-safe held-out evaluation, majority/median and ordinal baselines, per-grade error and uncertainty, and treat output first as a discrepancy *flag*, not judged placement. Shuffling labels is a useful negative control but does not define chance without a specified class distribution.

fact: Published difficulty model (CIPI) run on our files
reports: Henle-scale level 1-9 per file from the published model; its agreement with our published levels on the same files as D02.
definition: compute_difficulty(path) from Ramoneda et al. 2024 (Expert Systems with Applications), trained on 652 Henle-graded classical scores; reported ensemble result 39.5% exact over 9 levels and 87.3% within one level on its own test data (read through a summariser, not from the PDF).
implementation: Separate Python environment: the repository pins torch 2.0.1 with Linux-only CUDA and triton wheels and music21 8.3, so on this Windows machine it needs CPU torch and relaxed pins. Not easy; listed because it is the reuse-first option the owner asked us to look for.
library_and_prior_evidence: Code: github.com/PRamoneda/difficulty-prediction-CIPI, AGPL-3.0 (fine for personal use). Models ship in the package.
pitfalls: Trained on classical originals, so easy song arrangements are outside its data; Henle levels are not exam grades, so the mapping is measured on our files, not assumed.
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: runs on 20 chosen.csv files of known level and its order agrees with ours better than D02's. Fail: install fails or agreement is worse; dropped. Fool: a Grade 8 piece and a Level B piece must not come out the same level.
used_for: Same as D02
why_easy: NOT easy: listed for the owner's decision (medium; a one-off environment, then one function call per file).
chatgpt_independent_review: DEFER FROM EASY; OPTIONAL EXPERIMENT — External CIPI model exists and README exposes `compute_difficulty(path)` (verified on authors’ GitHub), but predictions are Henle 1–9 rather than our grades and the source test accuracy is 39.5% *balanced accuracy*, not 39.5% exact across an equivalent syllabus. The row’s 87.3% within-one figure is only secondhand here. A two-item fool check proves little. Try only after a small CPU inference feasibility check and comparable same-held-out evaluation against D02/simple baselines; do not distort the application dependency stack or force Windows CUDA pins. Check AGPL-3.0 obligations before shipping model/code or hosted service integration.
